Legal Standards.name: Endangered Species Act (ESA) / California Endangered Species Act (CESA)
Legal Standards.note: State and federal legislation providing primary legal protection for salmon and other listed species. ESA implementation requires Biological Opinions (BiOps), which carry the force of federal law and govern operations affecting endangered species.

key_elements.scope: Operational requirements for activities affecting listed species such as salmon

Legal Standards.name: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Legal Standards.note: Provides federal legal authority and oversight for the development, approval, and implementation of state and local water quality standards.

Legal Standards.name: California Water Code
Legal Standards.note: Statutory framework encompassing regulatory authorities that protect salmon populations indirectly through water management and more directly through protection of commercial and recreational fishing.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act (CWA) / Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act
Legal Standards.note: Establish the authority and scope of water quality regulation, including determination of covered waters. Temperature is explicitly addressed as a water quality parameter under this regulatory umbrella.

Legal Standards.name: Central Valley Project Improvement Act (CVPIA) / Anadromous Fish Restoration Program (AFRP)
Legal Standards.note: Requires population doubling of anadromous fish in Central Valley streams and mitigation of adverse impacts from CVP operations. Multiple environmental factors are implicated.

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Order 90-5 and USBR Temperature Management Plan
Legal Standards.note: Regulates USBR water releases to protect salmon, native fish, and habitat in the Sacramento and Trinity River Basins, with a primary focus on temperature control through reservoir operations.

Legal Standards.name: Delta Stewardship Council (DSC) Salinity Metrics
Legal Standards.note: Science-based salinity metrics developed under EPA authority to support water quality protection objectives.

Tier 1.policy_name: Reservoir releases & diversion management (%UIF, X2, temperature, salinity)
Tier 1.note: Managed largely through reservoir releases or changes in diversions; affects salmon and water availability, implicating curtailments in drier years. Water comes from aggregate storage, not individual rights holders.

Tier 1.policy_name: USFWS ESA BiOps for federal projects
Tier 1.note: Biological Opinions produced for projects potentially affecting listed species or critical habitat. Includes incidental take and mitigation measures; part of normal non-emergency water management.
Normal fishing season continues under Tier 1 conditions.

Tier 2.policy_name: Reservoir releases & diversion management (%UIF, X2, temperature, salinity)
Tier 2.note: Flow, salinity/X2, and temperature management continues as in Tier 1.
Fishing season likely reduced under Tier 2 conditions.

Tier 3.note: Doubled impacts on already diminished populations, addressed mainly through litigation and injunctive relief; includes flows, environmental review, CVP operations, and salmon habitat management.
Fishing season much reduced or eliminated under Tier 3 conditions.

Tier 4.note: Population collapse occurs; harm addressed through litigation as in Tier 3 but at a full emergency level.
